title: Raise default_statistics_target 300->500 for skewed GetUserTweets selectivity
configuration_cause: default_statistics_target=300 still leaves GetUserTweets (88% of terminal capacity, p50 175us, p95 512us) on a single Index Scan whose selectivity for skewed user_id predicates is estimated from a bounded histogram; the r006 100->300 step was tested but never isolated at the top of the safe range, and the planner cost model (random_page_cost 1.5, seq_page_cost 0.8) is already cache-consistent, so residual per-call page reads are a statistics-resolution limit rather than a cost-model limit.
mechanism: GetUserTweets dominates terminal time (0.88 of capacity) with p50 175us and p95 512us; the plan evidence shows a single Index Scan with estimated_rows=1.0. With skewed user_id distributions, a 300-target histogram/MCV list can misestimate the number of matching tweets per user, causing the executor to walk more index pages per call than necessary. Raising default_statistics_target to the safe maximum 500 increases histogram and MCV resolution for the skewed predicate, tightening estimated_rows and reducing pages touched per GetUserTweets call, which lowers p50/p95 and frees terminal capacity for higher successful TPS. This is a distinct amplitude from the refuted r006 100->300 step and is the only remaining in-scope planner lever not yet tested at its bound.
query_effect: Finer user_id histogram/MCV resolution tightens estimated_rows for the GetUserTweets predicate, reducing index pages walked per call and stabilizing the Index Scan path.
expected_tps_effect: Modest increase in successful_transaction_tps as GetUserTweets terminal occupancy falls; bounded because the plan is already an Index Scan.
expected_latency_effect: GetUserTweets p50 and p95 decrease; other transaction classes largely unchanged.

predictions.rationale: Higher statistics resolution reduces pages walked per GetUserTweets call, lowering median latency.
Tighter selectivity estimates reduce tail page walks for skewed users.
Lower GetUserTweets terminal occupancy frees capacity for more completed transactions.

alternatives.statement: If statistics resolution is not the limiter, raising random_page_cost further (1.5->2.5) would shift GetUserTweets off the Index Scan and change p50 without changing statistics.
If the residual limiter is WAL commit-path queueing rather than planner selectivity, GetUserTweets p50 stays flat while wal_waiting_backends.max remains 1 and sync_average_ms dominates.

why_exceeds_incumbent: Tests the untested top of the safe statistics range (500 vs incumbent 300) on the dominant transaction class; the r006 100->300 step was refuted but 500 is a distinct amplitude at the bound and the only remaining in-scope planner lever.

nodes.label: Finer user_id selectivity estimates reduce GetUserTweets pages per call

knob_changes.numerical_basis: Raise from incumbent 300 to the safe high bound 500 (allowed [50,500]); 1.67x histogram/MCV resolution for skewed user_id, distinct from the refuted r006 100->300 step.
knob_changes.mechanism_role: column statistics resolution for skewed predicate selectivity

cross_domain_requirements: memory_storage: keep WAL commit-path bundle stable so GetUserTweets latency change is attributable to statistics
